correctness.rationale: Coordinatewise extreme-point argument reduces vector suprema to r phases. On the circumference-pi lattice, any cluster of k columns has maximal contribution 2 sin(k pi/(2n))/sin(pi/(2n)), since the best k distances to one phase occur at k cyclic consecutive vertices and a midpoint phase attains the cosine sum. The maximum over all coordinate assignments is the maximum over integer partitions of n into at most r positive block lengths; sine is strictly increasing and concave here, so all s=min(r,n) coordinates are used and lengths differ by at most one. Consecutive balanced blocks realize all per-block upper bounds simultaneously. This yields exact formula, r=1 and r>=n boundary values, Jensen equality iff r|n for r<=n, and the explicit O_r(n^-3) Taylor residue deficit. An independently coded DP over all compositions plus explicit phase evaluation checked all 234 pairs 2<=n<=28, 1<=r<=min(n,10), including equality strictness. No finite grid substitutes for global continuous phase analysis.
